AP001.name: Public without explicit intent
AP001.description: Endpoint is public but lacks an explicit marker (like AllowAny) showing this was intentional. The scanner cannot tell if it's public by design or by mistake.
AP001.check_for: Explicit AllowAny permission, a public marker/decorator, or documentation showing the endpoint is intentionally public
AP001.false_positive_if: Endpoint is genuinely meant to be public by design (home page, static content, public catalog/reference data, login/register pages, health checks). NOT a false positive if: the endpoint exposes user-specific data, performs sensitive actions, or being public was an oversight.

AP002.name: Anonymous on write
AP002.description: A write endpoint (POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH) is explicitly marked AllowAny, permitting anonymous users to change state.
AP002.check_for: Whether AllowAny is intentional, or if the write should require authentication
AP002.false_positive_if: The write endpoint is genuinely meant to be anonymous by design (public registration, anonymous feedback form, public webhook receiver, login/token-check endpoints). NOT a false positive if: the write modifies protected resources, user data, or system state that should require login.

AP003.name: Auth conflict
AP003.description: A method-level AllowAny overrides the class-level authentication, creating an inconsistency where one method bypasses the auth the rest of the class enforces.
AP003.check_for: Whether the method-level override is intentional and documented, or an accidental security gap
AP003.false_positive_if: The override is intentional and the specific method is genuinely meant to be public (e.g. a public list on an otherwise protected viewset). NOT a false positive if: the override accidentally exposes a sensitive operation.

AP004.name: Missing auth on writes
AP004.description: A write endpoint (POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH) has no authentication configuration at all - not even an explicit AllowAny. State-changing operations are unprotected.
AP004.check_for: Any authentication: login_required, permission_classes, middleware auth, JWT validation on the write endpoint
AP004.false_positive_if: Auth is genuinely applied at a parent level (blueprint, router, middleware) that the scanner did not see, or the write is intentionally public (rare). NOT a false positive if: the endpoint truly has no auth and modifies data - this is Critical for a reason. A route name containing the word public does NOT make a missing-auth write safe.

AP005.name: Excessive roles
AP005.description: This is a DESIGN issue, NOT an authentication issue. The endpoint requires MORE THAN 3 ROLES, which may indicate overly complex or poorly designed authorization. The endpoint IS protected - the concern is only the NUMBER of roles, not whether auth exists.
AP005.check_for: Count the roles. Are all of them genuinely needed and distinct, or are some redundant, duplicated, or leftovers? Do NOT evaluate whether the endpoint has authentication - it does. Only judge if the role COUNT is justified.
AP005.false_positive_if: All listed roles are legitimate and serve genuinely distinct user types that each need access (e.g. admin, manager, analyst, viewer for a reports page where each role really views reports). NOT a false positive if: roles are duplicated, redundant, or the long list signals a design problem. IMPORTANT: do not answer based on authentication - this alarm is purely about whether having this many roles is justified.

AP006.name: Weak role naming
AP006.description: This is a DESIGN/NAMING issue, NOT an authentication issue. One or more roles use generic names like user or admin that do not clearly describe the permission scope. The endpoint IS protected - the concern is only the role NAMING, not whether auth exists.
AP006.check_for: Look at the role NAMES. Are they specific and descriptive of the actual permissions, or vague generic words? Do NOT evaluate whether the endpoint has authentication - it does. Only judge the clarity of the role names.
AP006.false_positive_if: The generic name is an established, well-understood convention in this codebase (e.g. admin universally means full access here). NOT a false positive if: the vague naming genuinely causes confusion about what the role can access. IMPORTANT: do not answer based on authentication - this alarm is purely about role-name clarity.

AP007.name: Sensitive keywords
AP007.description: A public route contains sensitive keywords like admin, debug, or export, suggesting it may expose privileged functionality without protection.
AP007.check_for: Whether the route with sensitive keywords actually has authentication despite being flagged public
AP007.false_positive_if: The keyword appears coincidentally and the route is genuinely safe to be public (e.g. /admin-login which is the login page itself). NOT a false positive if: the route exposes admin/debug/export functionality without auth.

AP008.name: Endpoint without auth
AP008.description: Endpoint has no authentication configuration at all - the scanner found no auth markers, decorators, or permission classes.
AP008.check_for: Any auth configuration: decorators, permission_classes, middleware, framework-level auth
AP008.false_positive_if: The endpoint is public by design (home page, static content, public catalog/reference data, login pages), or auth is applied at a parent level (blueprint/router/middleware) the scanner did not detect. NOT a false positive if: the endpoint serves protected data or actions with genuinely no auth.
